title: Senior Data Analyst, CS Commercial Operations
Senior Email Developer: Future Opportunities
description:
A note before you apply
We're not actively hiring for this role today, but we're building relationships ahead of upcoming client work. If your background fits, we'd like to start a conversation now so we're ready to move when a project lands!
Who We Are
Stitch is the global leader in helping brands drive CRM performance through Braze and Databricks. We work with Fortune 1000 brands to design and execute martech-driven solutions and lifecycle marketing strategies that drive meaningful outcomes. Our fast-growing team spans the US, UK, and Canada.
We’re actively building the best customer relationship marketing (CRM) consultancy in the world. Not the biggest-the best. We’re looking for teammates who are energized by this challenge.
The Role
As a Senior Technical Producer (our term for an email developer!), you bridge campaign management and complex implementation. You own advanced Liquid development, Connected Content integrations, multi-channel Canvas builds, landing page development, and advanced Catalog use cases. As AI becomes more dominant in the development community, you are able to leverage AI-tools to gain efficiencies, reverse-engineer scripting languages during platform migrations, build dynamic content solutions, and lead discovery sessions that uncover requirements gaps before they become project risks. You mentor Consultant Technical Producers, set quality standards through your own work, and bring a point of view to every client conversation.
Who You Are
First and foremost, you’re motivated by impact. To be the best CRM consultancy in the world, we have to be motivated by performance-both in how our work drives outcomes for our customers, and for how our work drives outcomes for Stitch.
This means you’re not content with status quo-you’re always looking towards what’s next and seeking opportunities to grow yourself, grow our customers, and grow Stitch. You have relentless standards and uphold them unapologetically. You move nimbly, take ownership, drive things forward, and make the people around you better. If this sounds like you, you will thrive here.
What You’ll Do

• Lead technical execution: multi-step Canvas builds with AI features, advanced segmentation, Connected Content integrations.

• Develop advanced Liquid: looping, nested conditionals, attribute segmentation, Connected Content calls, AI personalization tools.

• Build advanced Catalog use cases: exclusion lists, language translations, renderable content, preference center integration.

• Own landing page development-front-end HTML + CSS following best practices.

• Support or own gamification content development (In-App Messaging).

• Reverse-engineer scripting languages (AmpScript, HubL) for platform migration projects.

• Lead discovery sessions, identify requirements gaps, and recommend KPIs.

• Create client-ready documentation with 0-1 review cycles. Build internal templates.

• Mentor Consultant Technical Producers on methodology, platform best practices, and client communication.

• Manage your time to meet billable targets of 36+ hours per week.

• Travel up to 20% for client meetings, workshops, and onsite engagements.

What Success Looks Like

• Clients trust your technical judgment enough to give you autonomy.

• Your solutions push the boundaries of what clients thought was possible in Braze.

• Consultant Technical Producers you work with are leveling up because of your mentorship.

• You identify ways to add value and deepen client engagements

Requirements

• 5-9 years of marketing technology consulting experience or applicable experience in email marketing and campaign development.

• Advanced HTML, CSS, and Liquid proficiency.

• Experience with marketing automation or customer engagement platforms. Braze experience is a plus, especially in email creation using Braze’s Drag and Drop Editor

• Client-facing experience within an agency or consultancy required. Experience mentoring junior team members.

• Advanced proficiency in AI code

title: Senior AI Developer
description:

Euna Solutions is seeking a talented Senior AI Developer to be a key participant in our ambitious AI transformation of our finance platform for local and state government agencies. We are raising the bar on every part of the development process with an intentional agentic focus. This isn’t an idea, it’s accelerating taking what we have already achieved to the next level and it’s a great opportunity for an innovative curious AI developer who wants to push the boundaries and learn and work with some incredible talent.
The idea is to take this to the next level building applications with AI capabilities from the ground up. We need developers who know what good looks like, not just the code but all the other considerations necessary for building and designing enterprise grade software.
You'll own the hard problems: orchestration patterns that hold up under real-world load, developer experiences that let your teammates move fast with confidence, and engineering decisions that turn ambiguous requirements into concrete, operable systems.

Platform Ownership

• Own the evolution of shared AI components, libraries, and platform capabilities the whole team builds on. You set the bar for reliability, testability, and developer experience - not as a reviewer, but as the person who ships it.
AI Feature Development

• Design and build AI-powered product features end-to-end: LLM orchestration, prompt engineering workflows, evaluation, and observability. Carry work from requirements shaping through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
Delivery Systems

Mentorship & Growth

• Actively grow the engineers around you. Run technical reviews, establish best practices, and create an environment where the team can move quickly without constantly second-guessing their decisions.

• 7+ years of hands-on software development, with deep proficiency in at least one modern backend or full-stack language and breadth across the full SDLC

• Previous experience building scalable multi-tenant SaaS applications ideally in one of C#, Ruby, Rails, Elixir, Python or similar language.

ImpactAssets is a $5B nonprofit impact investing leader founded in 2010. Over the years, ImpactAssets has built an extensive impact investment platform, having invested in 1500+ private companies and impact funds addressing the world’s greatest challenges. ImpactAssets Capital Partners was created in 2022 to bring the ImpactAssets platform and customized investment services to institutional investors.
ImpactAssets and ImpactAssets Capital Partners together are catalyzing investment capital into mission-driven business models solving the worlds’ biggest challenges. The result? A fast growing, dynamic organization with an activated community of more than 1,800 clients. This level of growth, vision and commitment equals great opportunities to grow a career at ImpactAssets . title: AI Data Readiness Lead
description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset-AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Analytics is only as trustworthy as the definitions underneath it. As more reporting and decision-making moves to AI agents, the cost of ambiguous or conflicting metric definitions compounds, an agent applies the wrong rule confidently, at scale, and nobody catches it.

This role exists to prevent that. You will own what our numbers mean, make those definitions enforceable in the systems that serve them, and verify that both people and agents are using them.

This is a governance-first role with real technical depth. You will spend your time defining, implementing, and validating, building pipelines and developing agentic reporting are secondary.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

Own the metric registry. Establish canonical definitions for the metrics the business runs on. Where competing versions exist, convene the owners, document the disagreement, and drive to a decision. Publish changes with a clear statement of what moves and why.

Make definitions enforceable. Implement agreed definitions in the semantic layer and data catalog so they are applied by the system rather than described in a document. Retire superseded versions.

Reduce the surface area. Audit the reporting estate, retire assets with no audience, and establish ownership for what remains.

Build data quality checks/agents. Freshness, uniqueness, referential integrity, and cross-system reconciliation - with failures routed to named owners/agents who act on them.

Verify AI agents. Maintain an inventory of agents accessing company data and the definitions each relies on. Evaluate agent output against known-correct answers and track accuracy, refusal, and error rates.

Enable self-serve. Make governed data accessible and trustworthy for people querying it directly or through AI tools.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 5+ years in analytics, analytics engineering, or a closely related field

- Strong SQL, including comfort reverse-engineering undocumented transformation logic written by others

- Direct ownership of a semantic or metrics layer in production - dbt, Cube, LookML, or equivalent. Not just usage: responsibility for what went into it and w

title: Financial Controller
description:
About the Role

We are looking for a financial operator to be the source of truth for Telos Media . You will own the books across four entities and several creative brands, and you will use what you find there to tell leadership where the money is going. The mandate is simple: make the books bulletproof, then tell us what they mean.

This is a dual role. You need to be comfortable wearing both hats, and the second one is what makes this a Controller rather than an accountant:

•
The accounting hat. You own the general ledger. You ensure compliance, accuracy, and a close that lands on time every month.

•
The analyst hat. You own the insight. You explain why a brand is profitable or bleeding, using data you personally verified.

What You'll Do

1. Financial reporting and control

•
GL ownership. Prepare the final general ledger and P&L across all entities for the Head of Finance to sign off. If it is in the books, you vouch for it.

•
The close. Run a disciplined monthly close so leadership receives the financial package (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) by the 10th.

•
Review and quality control. Review the Finance Officer's reconciliations and expense coding. You are the first line of defence against errors reaching leadership.

•
Balance sheet hygiene. A clean balance sheet with no unreconciled suspense accounts and no unexplained transactions.

•
Multi-entity and intercompany. Maintain intercompany balances across US, UK and merchandise entities, and keep the intercompany position clean and reconcilable.

2. FP&A and strategic insight

•
Cost allocation. Build and maintain the logic mapping shared overhead (finance, HR, leadership) to specific brands. The measure is an accurate net profit per brand.

•
Variance analysis. Lead the monthly forecast-versus-actual review. Do not report the difference; explain the driver behind it.

•
Bleed analysis. Deep dives into struggling or new ventures to identify exactly where cash is leaking.

•
Channel P&L. Maintain individual P&Ls for creative channels so unit economics are visible.

•
Cash forecasting. Support the rolling cash forecast across entities, including inventory and production commitments.

About You

•
Experience. 5 or more years in accounting and finance, with real exposure to multi-entity or multi-currency environments. Startup, outsourced-accounting or SME background is a strong fit; large-corporate-only experience often is not.

•
Technical stack. Deep Xero proficiency is non-negotiable, including chart-of-accounts design and multi-entity handling. Expert Google Sheets or Excel - pivot tables, lookups, and building a model from scratch rather than filling one in.

•
Certification. CPA, CMA or equivalent preferred, not required where operational depth is strong.

•
Investigative instinct. This is the differentiator and we screen hard for it. You do not just categorise transactions. If a margin moves 2%, you find out why before anyone asks. If a number looks wrong, you say so, including to people senior to you.

•
Communication. You can explain a financial result to a non-finance founder in plain language, and defend it when challenged.

What Makes This Role Worth Taking

• Full ownership of finance across four entities and several brands, with no layer between you and the Head of Finance.

• Direct exposure to the CEO and General Manager. Your analysis reaches them in the month you produce it, not a quarter later.

• Genuine breadth. Accounting, FP&A, multi-currency, inventory, production financing and international structuring in one role.

• A finance function being built rather than maintained. You will shape how it works.

We are a fast-growing, multi-site aerospace company preparing for our first compliance program. We are seeking an experienced Compliance Manager to design, build, and lead the implementation of a unified Quality Management System (QMS) across all company locations. title: FinOps Engineer
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're looking for a FinOps Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams.

This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the Terraform or Lambda that ships the fix, working on a product feature chasing a number until it reconciles, and influencing product decisions when cost to reliability tradeoffs hit. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

- Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.

- Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.

- Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review.

- Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit.

- Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards engineering and finance can both read.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

- Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics.

- Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash

- Are comfortable with cost/billing tooling: AWS Cost Explorer, Cost & Usage Reports, GCP Billing Reports, and BI/dashboarding (we use Hex).

- Have experience with, or are comfortable picking up, Linear and Notion as the system of record for tracking and documenting FinOps work.

- Experience with a dedicated cloud cost management platform (e.g. CloudZero, Vantage, or similar) is a plus, not required.

- Can analyze cost data and present it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Have prior experience in a FinOps, cloud cost management, or cloud governance role.

- Are energized by doing the unglamorous, high-leverage work (the schlep) that unblocks other teams, and by working cross-functionally without positional authority.

Location: Remote, Americas (US, Canada, Latin America) | Travel: 10-20% to client sites
Why this role exists
Most enterprises don't have a cloud and AI cost problem. They have a deployment problem. They may already know their GPU fleet is oversubscribed, their inference bill is compounding, or parts of their estate are running inefficiently. What they often lack is someone who can walk into a risk-averse engineering organization, identify the highest-leverage change, solve the technical problem deeply enough to earn credibility, and get the change into production.
That is this job. Not analysis - optimization deployment.
We are hiring Sr Deployment Strategists because the constraint is no longer simply finding inefficiency. It is landing the fix inside a real organization, with real approval gates, tribal knowledge, and engineers who may not have asked for a vendor's opinion. You will own that journey from the first workshop through production change and measurable business impact.
What you'll own
Scope

• Partner with executive sponsors - CTO, VP Infrastructure, VP Engineering, Head of AI Platform - to turn ambiguous mandates into concrete, time-boxed deployments with a defensible business case.

• Lead technical discovery and architecture review. Surface integration complexity, infrastructure constraints, change-control realities and the technical tradeoffs that determine whether an engagement is feasible.

• Establish technical credibility quickly with customer engineering teams, challenge assumptions constructively, and say no to work that will not land.

title: Lead AI System Architect
description:
The AI System Architect leads the architecture of EIS's agentic AI platform - the design of multi-agent systems that automate insurance workflows end-to-end across Policy, Billing, and Claims domains. The role owns the patterns, frameworks, and standards for agent orchestration, MCP-based tool ecosystems, agent memory, planning, evaluation, and safety. RAG and conversational features are table stakes; the forward agenda is autonomous and semi-autonomous agents that act on behalf of users - quote intake, claims triage, underwriting and pricing intelligence, billing troubleshooting, and beyond - across our platform and technology stacks.
Key Responsibilities

• Own the architecture of EIS's agentic platform: agent orchestration, MCP-native tool ecosystems, agent memory (short-term, long-term, semantic), planning, and tool/function calling patterns reusable across product domains.

• Enable and provide support for domain teams for vertical insurance agents and the horizontal capabilities (RAG, retrieval, instructional flows) they compose from.

• Define and enforce levels of autonomy - assistive, semi-autonomous, autonomous - with explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, escalation paths, and reversibility for high-stakes actions in regulated workflows.

• Drive the MCP strategy: which capabilities EIS exposes as MCP servers to internal and partner agents, how our agents consume external MCP tools, and the tool registry, schemas, and versioning that keep this scalable.

• Maintain the multiple stack approach as a first-class capability: Typescript, and Java. Help teams to pick the right stack per agent and keep all aligned through shared configuration artefacts, prompt management, and evaluation tooling.

• Lead Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for agentic capabilities; partner with Platform, Security/InfoSec, and DevOps so agents are observable, testable, sandboxed, and compliant by default.

• Set safe-AI standards for agentic systems: prompt injection and tool-poisoning defenses, action allow-lists, blast-radius controls, PII handling, data residency, and bias mitigation. Treat agent safety as a first-class architectural concern.

• Translate insurance use cases into production agent designs with product strategists and domain architects; provide technical leadership and mentorship; communicate agentic trade-offs (autonomy, reliability, cost, safety) clearly to executives, customers, and engineers.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

• Proven track record designing and shipping agentic systems in production - not demos, not prototypes - with meaningful autonomy and multi-step tool use.

• Strong systems background: data-intensive, distributed, and latency-sensitive design in production environments.

Sharp instinct for when an agent is the right answer and when a deterministic workflow is. Tracks the frontier and translates what matters into the roadmap.

• Strong with the Java/Spring ecosystem.

• Strong with Typescript and Python for AI (LangChain, LangGraph, or equivalent agent framework) - production experience required. Equally comfortable in both stacks.

• Hands-on with vector databases including embedding models, hybrid search, re-ranking, and retrieval evaluation.

• Experience with agent evaluation and observability: traces, replays, eval harnesses, guardrails, and cost/latency telemetry. Familiar with AI configuration-as-code.

• Experience shipping AI services on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) in regulated enterprise environments - security review, data residency, audit trails.

Co tě u nás čeká?

title: Builder
description:
About SafeLease

At SafeLease , we're rethinking how P&C insurance is sold in an age of technological change. We believe the industry's biggest inefficiencies aren't technical problems - they're structural ones. And we're building the team to tackle them.
SafeLease is a profitable insurance business that designs, underwrites, and distributes specialty coverage for commercial property owners and their tenants. Most insurance companies either distribute products or bear the risk - we do both. We back our policies with our own capital, which means we control the full stack: product design, tech, and the speed at which we move. That end-to-end ownership lets us offer customers real flexibility, saving time and money for more than 4,000 properties insured for billions in value nationwide.
We're a team of 85, growing over 100% annually, and we've done it without sacrificing profitability or culture. Here, you'll get high discretion and a wide aperture of problems to solve. We embrace the newest technologies, move fast together, and operate with the intensity of a small company where every person's work is visible. If you're looking for a place to sharpen your craft alongside people who take their work seriously, you'll fit right in.
Why "Builder"?
The best people on our team start with a business problem, figure out what should exist to solve it, and then build it, often end-to-end. They talk to stakeholders, sketch out solutions, make product and design decisions, write the code, and ship it. They use AI tools not as a novelty but as a core part of how they work. The line between "product thinking" and "engineering" isn't one they spend much time drawing.
We call this role Builder because that's what it actually is. You'll work in small pods with a GM who sets direction, but how you get there and what you build along the way is largely up to you.
If you're looking for a well-defined backlog and a narrow lane, this probably isn't the right fit. If you want the autonomy to solve real problems and the context to understand why they matter, keep reading.
About the Role
To drive our mission forward, this role will:

• Start with the problem, not the ticket. Understand the business context behind what you're building. Know why it matters to customers, to the business, and to the team.

• Own outcomes, not just output. Take features from idea to production. That means participating in product and design decisions, not waiting for a spec to land in your lap.

• Build across the full stack. Write clean, maintainable code across frontend, backend, and infrastructure with a focus on reliability, performance, and simplicity.

• Use AI as a force multiplier. Leverage AI-powered tools to move faster, explore solutions more broadly, and spend your time on the problems that actually require human judgment.

• Improve the system, not just your code. Identify opportunities to make the platform better, the team faster, and the product sharper. Bring ideas, not just implementations.

• Collaborate with high context. Work closely with your pod, leadership, and cross-functional partners. Share what you know, ask what you don't.

About You
You're a problem solver who happens to write code, not the other way around. You care about what gets built as much as how it gets built. You're comfortable with ambiguity, energized by ownership, and sharp enough to develop a working understanding of the business you're building for.
Your experience:

• 2-5+ years of experience in full-stack software development with a track record of shipping real-world applications

• Background in CS/EE, a coding bootcamp, or equivalent hands-on experience building production systems

• Proficiency across Frontend (TypeScript, JavaScript, React), Backend (Node.js, Express.js, REST APIs), and Infrastructure (relational databases, Git, AWS)

• Demonstrated fluency with AI-powered development tools (Cursor, Claude, Copilot, etc.) - not just awareness, but active use in your workflow

title: Senior Manager, Royalty Administration & Onboarding
description:
Established in 2015, Create Music Group is a leading music and entertainment company. The company operates as a record label, distribution company, and entertainment network which generates over 15 billion music streams each month on DSP’s. Named #2 on the Inc 5000 Fastest Growth Companies in America in 2020, the company has grown exponentially by leveraging its owned IP with its media and technology platform. The company works with superstar artists, major and independent record labels, and global media brands. It operates a number of companies including Label Engine, one of the largest independent music distribution platforms in the world, with over 75,000 artists and 5,000 label clients; and Flighthouse, a digital entertainment brand focused on Gen Z, which has more than 300 million followers across social media. Create Music Group is based in Hollywood, CA and has 400 employees worldwide.

Job Summary

At Create Music Group , acquiring a catalog is only the beginning. The next step is turning each acquisition into a fully operational royalty business - accurately configured, scalable, and built to serve artists, partners, and rightsholders for the long term.

The Senior Manager, Royalty Administration & Onboarding plays a critical role in making that happen. This leader oversees the royalty onboarding strategy for newly acquired catalogs, translating complex deal terms into clear, effective royalty structures and workflows across Create’s systems. From interpreting acquisition agreements to designing the future-state setup, this role ensures every catalog is positioned for accurate and efficient royalty administration from day one.

As a key partner to our M&A, Finance, Legal, and Royalties teams, the Senior Manager is involved early in the acquisition lifecycle-including during diligence-to identify royalty requirements, surface potential gaps, and help shape a seamless transition into Create’s platform. The role works closely with the Director of Royalties and leads a growing team responsible for bringing each onboarding strategy to life.

This is an opportunity to sit at the intersection of music rights, acquisitions, operations, and technology at a company that continues to expand its global catalog and platform. We’re looking for a leader who understands the details of royalty administration but can also see the bigger picture: how to build scalable processes, navigate complex deals, and create an exceptional foundation for every catalog that joins Create Music Group .

Responsibilities

• Own contract-to-system royalty interpretation company-wide: rates, splits, territories, escalators, cross-collateralization, recoupment, and defensible workarounds where a platform cannot implement a term literally.

• Own the Royalties Readiness Gate for incoming acquisitions. Issue the go/no-go recommendation on every acquisition before it enters statement processing, with peer review from the Senior Manager, Royalty Accounting & Operations.

• Own the handoff packet standard for incoming acquisitions. Every acquisition handoff states plainly what is final, what is assumed, and what remains open. No acquisition transfers to operations without one.

• Lead contractual royalty obligation analysis for acquisitions, including a written risk/reward recommendation on onboarding methodology - migrate the label into our systems, or leave it on its existing platform.

• Represent Royalties in M&A diligence from LOI. Own the royalty section of the diligence memo and the list of closing conditions Royalties depends on.

• Own the team's project portfolio: expense validation tooling, bulk and automated ingestion of expenses, sales, and contracts, the M&A onboarding checklist, and automated metadata, contract, and payor template generation derived from statement analysis.

• Own role-based access and configuration governance across all royalty systems. Define who may create clients, update splits, and alter contract terms - and enforce it.

At the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard University (CEPR) our mission is to transform education through the power of quality evidence. We believe that if we want to dramatically improve educational outcomes for all children, evidence must play a critical role.
The Math Teaching and Teacher Learning team at CEPR provides math-specific professional development to teachers and coaches to help improve math instruction. Our current grant-funded projects seek to develop and test an expanded math-specific coach training program (M-Powering Teacher Coaching) that uses machine-learning automated feedback and AI-enhanced coaching tools. The Data Scientist will contribute to this and other projects that connect rigorous educational research with practical tools for teachers, instructional coaches, and education leaders. This person will oversee, manage, and lead analysis and application of complex datasets, and contribute to the integration of research insights into innovative educational tools and cutting-edge products. They will be joining a team with faculty lead and Principal Investigator, Heather Hill, and collaborators at higher education research institutions, professional learning organizations, curriculum providers, and Enterprise AI firm(s).
